BLOCKER: gate0_check.py: the except handler calls `execution_trail.write_failure(...)`, but only the `trail` alias is bound inside the try → NameError crashes gate0 on any trail-write failure instead of degrading gracefully.

No `scripts/dev/execution_trail.py` exists although AC + docs/REVIEW-GATES-LIFECYCLE.md name it as owner; all 296 lines of logic (CLI, locking, rendering) live in `core/execution_trail.py`, inverting the required "thin adapter" architecture.

Stale-lock hazard: `_lock` uses O_EXCL with no pid/mtime reclaim; one crashed writer leaves `.lock` forever, so every subsequent write times out and permanently blocks the item's trail/completion gate.
MAJOR: Failure path violates AC: `backlog.set_status`/`set_delivery` swallow trail failures with a plain `print` (no structured `execution_trail_write_failed`, no `_failures.jsonl` sink); `precheck._record_trail`'s handler calls `trail.write_failure` when the import itself may be what failed → NameError in the handler.

`order_problems()` validates only design_review<gate1 and diff_review<gate2; AC requires ALL pre-merge stages be checked for order (planning→gate0→...→precheck), so out-of-order tests/precheck/implementation pass the gate.
`set_status`/`set_delivery` record `completion`/`delivery` even when the underlying `update()` returns None/fails — trail can assert a completion that never happened (integrity).

`precheck._record_trail` records stage `tests` as "pass" when the tests list is empty (`all([])` is True), satisfying the required `tests` stage with zero tests; it also re-appends code_review/tests/precheck events on every run (unbounded append growth).

New shipped logic (296 lines, file locking, CLI, subprocess rendering) lands in the `core/` shipped root via an `allow_new_python` governance edit rather than Go or a genuinely thin adapter — bypasses the language-rule intent the config itself flags as a governance change.
MINOR: `_path` regex requires a middle segment (`BI-XX-123`) while backlog's `_BARE_BI_RE` allows `BI-123`; valid bare ids would raise and fail the completion gate.
`show()` sorts by stage rank, not `seq`, so duplicate stage events are rendered out of sequence vs the AC's "ordered trail".
Usage section never renders the literal "not captured" when no usage was captured (AC), only a `not_captured=0` counter.
`gate_decisions` records `f"gate{gate}"`; any non-integer gate value (e.g. "1.5") is an unknown stage → guaranteed write failure.
Duplicate wiring: `execution-trail` is in precheck `_GATES` (tier "post") and also run unconditionally after the gate loop → double execution or a dead entry.
`refs` dicts are persisted unredacted (redaction covers only `summary`/`actor`).
`execution_trail_check` couples to private APIs `g2.ar._get_item` and `g2._git`; brittle across refactors.
NIT: `print(f"\n=== precheck: execution-trail ===")` unnecessary f-string; unused `import json` inside `_record_trail`'s try.
gate0: `if a.report: continue` is dead code (the report path returns earlier).
store-registry key `trails/<ID>.json` vs AC path `engineering/trails/<ITEM>.json` naming inconsistency.
SUMMARY: Solid shape overall (append-only store, redaction, tests, gate wiring), but the error-handling paths are broken (NameError in two failure handlers, silent prints instead of the AC-mandated structured event), the ordering check is materially weaker than the AC requires, and the module placement contradicts the documented thin-adapter/language-rule contract.
Top risks: a trail-write failure crashing gates instead of reporting it, stale locks permanently blocking completions, and `tests`/`completion` stages being satisfiable without real evidence.
